source: Pagelence 项目编写：词汇、语法与十五篇原创短文；题目只用于应用内参考评级，不作认证。

passages.title: The Lost Ticket
passages.text:
Ben was going to visit his grandmother on Saturday. She lived in a small town by the sea, and the train took about two hours. His mother gave him a ticket and said, "Keep it in your pocket."

At the station, the wind was strong. Ben took the ticket out to read the number of his seat, and a big gust pulled it from his hand. The ticket flew across the platform and stopped under a bench. Ben ran after it, but a man with a big bag stepped in front of him, and the ticket was gone.

Ben's face went red. He had no money for a second ticket. A woman in a blue coat saw him looking under the benches. "Are you looking for this?" she asked. She was holding his ticket. The wind had carried it to the other end of the platform, and she had caught it.

Ben thanked her many times. On the train, he put the ticket inside his book, not in his pocket. When he arrived, his grandmother was waiting at the gate with a smile. Ben told her the story, and she laughed. "Next time," she said, "take a photo of it too."

passages.title: Moving Day
passages.text:
On Friday morning, Leo's family moved to a new flat on the other side of the city. There were twelve boxes in the living room, and Leo could not find his school bag. "It is in the blue box," said his mother. She was right, but the blue box was under three heavy ones.

At noon, a woman from the flat next door knocked at the door. Her name was Mrs Bell, and she brought a warm apple cake. "Welcome to the building," she said. Leo's father made tea for everyone, and they sat on the floor because the chairs were still in the truck.

In the afternoon, Leo went to look for the cat. Mimi was not in the kitchen or in the bedroom. At last he found her in an empty box near the window, asleep on his old jacket. She looked very comfortable.

In the evening, the family ate pizza on the balcony and watched the lights of the city. Leo missed his old street, but the new flat had a bigger window and a small garden. "We can plant tomatoes here," his father said. Leo smiled. Maybe the new place was not so bad after all.

passages.title: A Rainy Saturday
passages.text: Saturday morning was grey and wet. Emma wanted to go to the park with her dog, but the rain did not stop. She made a cup of tea and looked out of the window. Then she had an idea. She put on her old coat and took an umbrella. The dog jumped up and down when he saw the coat. They walked to the small cafe near the river. Emma had a warm sandwich, and the dog sat under the table. By the time they went home, the rain had stopped. Emma was happy: it was a good day after all.

passages.title: The Spring Clean-up
passages.text:
Last Saturday our street held its first spring clean-up, and I almost did not go. I had planned to stay in bed with a book, but my neighbour Ana knocked at eight o'clock with two pairs of gloves and a bright orange bag.

About thirty people met in the small square behind the library. A retired teacher, Mr Doyle, gave each group a map and a list of streets. Our group of six was sent to the river path, where rubbish collects after the winter floods. I expected the work to be dull, but the morning passed quickly. We pulled bottles, old shoes and even a broken chair out of the water. A boy of about ten found a bicycle wheel and shouted as if he had won a prize.

By noon we had filled twelve bags. The bakery on the corner brought bread and hot tea, and we sat on the grass talking to people we had passed in the street for years without ever speaking.

Nothing dramatic happened, and nobody thanked us in public. Yet when I walked past the river the next morning and saw the clean water moving between the stones, I understood why Ana had knocked on my door.

passages.title: A New Start at Forty
passages.text:
For eleven years I worked in the same office, checking invoices for a company that sold office furniture. The work was steady, the pay was reasonable, and I could do it with my eyes half closed. That was exactly the problem.

When the company announced that our department would move to another city, my colleagues were worried. I was surprised to find that I felt almost relieved. I had been thinking about a change for two years, but I had never said it aloud, because it sounded ungrateful.

I spent three months learning to use design software at a local college, two evenings a week. The first class was awful. Everyone else seemed to understand the instructions at once, and I went home convinced that forty was too late to start again. My teacher, however, told me to stop comparing myself with people who had been doing it for years.

In June I applied for a job at a small studio that designs signs for shops. I did not get it. In July I applied again, after they advertised a second post, and this time they said yes. The pay is lower and the office is noisy. I still arrive early every morning, but now I arrive because I want to.

passages.title: Two Days in a Quiet Town
passages.text:
My friend Ruth and I chose the town of Marlow for a weekend because the guidebook called it 'peaceful'. It did not mention the bus, which came twice a day and stopped running at six.

We arrived on Friday evening with two small bags and a list of places to see. The first thing we discovered was that the museum closed at four, and the second was that the only restaurant open was a pizza place beside the station. We ate there twice in two days, and I am not sorry.

On Saturday morning we walked along the river to an old stone bridge. A man was fishing, and he told us, without being asked, about the winter the river froze and the year the bridge was repaired. He talked for half an hour. Ruth kept looking at her watch, but I did not want him to stop.

The town had no cinema, no shopping centre and almost no traffic. By Sunday afternoon we had read our books twice and knew the name of the woman who ran the bakery. On the bus home, Ruth said she had been bored for two whole days. I said I had not been bored for a single minute, and we both laughed, because we were both right.

passages.title: Saving the Second-hand Shelves
passages.text:
The workshop behind the library smells of glue and old paper. Twice a week, six volunteers sit at a long table and repair books that readers have damaged or that have simply fallen apart. Most are ordinary paperbacks: a cookbook with a broken spine, a novel whose pages have come loose, a dictionary that someone dropped in the bath.

The project began almost by accident. A retired teacher brought in a box of books she could not bear to throw away, and the librarian admitted that the library itself was quietly discarding dozens every month. Repairing them seemed cheaper than replacing them, and it kept titles on the shelf that no longer exist in print.

Volunteers take a short training course, and the rules are strict. They never repair anything valuable; a book worth more than fifty pounds goes to a professional. They use reversible glue, so that a later owner can undo their work. And they record every repair in a notebook, because, as the teacher puts it, a book with a history should not lose it.

Last year the workshop saved more than four hundred books. The library now lends them with a small card inside, explaining what was done, so that readers understand why a repaired copy sometimes looks older than it is.

passages.title: The Noise After Dark
passages.text:
Every summer the argument returns to our street. Some residents want the bars along the waterfront to close at eleven; others say the music is what keeps the district alive. Last month the council asked both sides to submit written statements, and the responses were sharper than anyone had expected.

Those who want earlier closing times talk about the health of people who work early shifts. A nurse who lives above one of the bars told the council that she has not slept properly in three years. Her neighbours describe broken glass, shouting and taxis waiting with their engines running until two in the morning. For them the issue is not culture but ordinary rest.

The bar owners answer that the district was quiet and poor before the music arrived, and that visitors now pay for the street lighting, the rubbish collection and the bus that runs after midnight. They also note that the loudest complaints come from buildings that were converted into flats only five years ago, when the bars were already there.

The council has not decided yet. It has, however, asked for one thing that nobody objects to: a proper measurement of the noise, taken at night, over a whole season. Until those figures exist, both sides are arguing about impressions.

passages.title: Working from Home
passages.text: Ten years ago, working from home was unusual. Today many companies offer it, and employees often say they are more productive without the commute. But the picture is not entirely positive. A recent survey found that people who work alone at home miss the informal conversations that used to happen in an office. Those conversations often produce new ideas, and they also make it easier to ask for help. Some companies have tried to solve the problem by asking staff to come in two or three days a week. Others have given up their offices completely and rely on video calls. Neither approach suits everyone. What seems clear is that the office is no longer the only place where work happens; the question is what it is still good for.

passages.title: A Quiet Exhibition That Refuses to Explain Itself
passages.text:
The new exhibition at the City Gallery, Fragments of a Working Life, gathers some ninety objects from the estate of a factory inspector who died in 1978. There are no wall texts beyond names and dates; the curator has deliberately left the labels bare.

This will infuriate visitors who expect to be told what to think. It also, for about half an hour, works remarkably well. A worn leather satchel, a tin of blunt pencils and a stack of notebooks in three different hands acquire a strange weight when nothing explains them. The notebooks are the centre of the show: page after page of measurements, and, in the margins, small drawings of birds.

Then the silence begins to feel like a mannerism. Without context the objects cannot build a story, only an atmosphere, and an hour of atmosphere is a long hour. The final room, which does offer a short timeline, is easily the most interesting space in the building, and its brevity looks less like a stylistic choice than an admission.

Still, this is a thoughtful, carefully made exhibition, and the risk it takes is worth more than the polished certainties of the gallery's previous show. Go, and take someone who will argue with you about it.

passages.title: A Study, a Headline and a Missing Clause
passages.text:
On Tuesday morning a national newspaper announced that screen time damages teenagers' memory. By lunchtime the claim had been repeated on three radio programmes; by evening it was being quoted in a school newsletter. The trouble is that the study it referred to said nothing of the kind.

The research, which followed 1,200 pupils for two years, found a modest correlation between evening screen use and lower scores on a single vocabulary test. The authors were careful. They noted that the effect disappeared once bedtime and sleep length were taken into account, and they warned explicitly that no causal link could be drawn from their data. That warning sits in the fourth paragraph of the paper, and in none of the coverage.

None of this is new. Journalists work to deadlines, press offices need headlines, and a correlation of minus 0.08 sounds far less alarming than a threat to memory. What is newer is the speed at which a simplified claim travels, and how hard it is to correct once it has settled into a school newsletter.

The lead author now spends part of each week answering emails from parents who want to know whether they should ban tablets. Her answer, familiar and unglamorous, is that sleep, conversation and a sensible bedtime matter more than the device itself.

passages.title: Telemedicine After the Emergency
passages.text:
During the pandemic most health systems discovered, almost overnight, that a great deal of routine care could be delivered by video call. Consultations that had once required an hour of travel and a morning off work became a fifteen-minute conversation. Many patients, especially those in rural areas, would like to keep it that way.

The policy question is not whether telemedicine works; the evidence on that is reasonably encouraging for follow-ups, long-term conditions and mental health support. The question is who pays for it, and on what terms. At present clinics are reimbursed at the same rate for a video appointment as for a face-to-face one, which makes the cheaper option the more profitable one. That is not a scandal in itself, but it does mean that convenience, rather than clinical need, may begin to decide the format of care.

There are quieter costs too. A physical examination cannot be conducted through a screen, and some diagnoses simply require a hand on the patient. Two health boards have started requiring a face-to-face review after three consecutive remote appointments, a rule that sounds bureaucratic until you read the case notes.

The sensible position is neither enthusiasm nor nostalgia. Telemedicine should be treated as one tool among several, chosen for the right patient and paid for in a way that does not reward whoever happens to own the better camera.

passages.title: The Algorithm Knows What You Liked Yesterday
passages.text:
For a while the promise was flattering: a library that never sleeps, tuned to your taste. What the recommender actually learns, however, is not your taste but your history of compromises. It sees the film you finished on a delayed flight and the one you abandoned after eleven minutes, and it cannot tell which was the accident. It rewards what you have already chosen, then calls the result your identity.

The trouble is not that the machine is wrong about us. It is that it is right about a version of us we did not mean to become. Taste is largely a record of what we have been exposed to; expose a person to one narrow stream and their preferences will duly narrow, and the system will report the narrowing as discovery. A recommendation engine is, in this sense, a mirror that flatters by agreeing.

Critics often ask for transparency: show us the weights, publish the model. Useful, but insufficient. I would rather the systems be built to be a little disappointing — to serve the occasional thing you did not ask for, the film from a country you have never visited, the record that takes three listens. A culture that only ever receives what it has already approved will be efficient, and it will be smaller.

passages.title: Keep the Shabby Corner
passages.text:
There is a fashion in preservation, and it currently favours the museum. A district is saved, scrubbed, lit from below, and let to a chain of coffee shops; its history is printed on a small enamel plate that nobody stops to read. We call this rescue. The neighbours who used it as a market, a shortcut, a place to sit, are not consulted, and after the rents double they are no longer there to be consulted.

I am not arguing against repair. Roofs fail, and a city that lets its buildings rot is not being romantic, merely negligent. But preservation has two possible objects: the fabric of a place, or the life that happens in it. The first can be secured with money. The second requires something less photogenic — rent controls, a lease for the cobbler, a bench where the bench used to be, an unglamorous exemption from the rules that make a corner shop unviable.

The test is easy to apply and rarely applied. Ask what the district is like on a wet Tuesday in February. If the answer is a locked door and a laminated menu, we have preserved a photograph, not a neighbourhood. Heritage is not the building; it is the habit of using it. Keep the shabby corner, and the rest may follow.

passages.title: The Shape We Give to Memory
passages.text:
Every memoir is a quiet argument about what a life is. The writer sifts a decade for the hour that explains it, and the hour, once chosen, begins to rearrange everything around itself. This is not dishonesty; it is the cost of coherence. A memory that has never been told is a clutter of impressions, some vivid, most already fading at the edges. Tell it once and it acquires a shape: a beginning that promises, a middle that complicates, an end that forgives.

What troubles me is how quickly the shape hardens. I have returned to the same afternoon in my own account of it for thirty years, and I no longer know whether I remember the afternoon or the telling. The detail I trust most — a green door, a smell of coal — may be a detail I invented because the story needed an anchor. Narrative is a generous host and an unreliable witness.

None of this makes the memoir worthless. We do not read them for the record; we read them for the reckoning. A writer who admits that the door may have been blue is more trustworthy than one who is certain of everything, because the first has noticed the machinery and the second has mistaken it for the world.

questions.prompt: She {{blank}} to school every day.

explanation.zh: 一般现在时第三人称单数，动词加 -s。
explanation.en: Simple present, third person singular: the verb takes -s.

questions.prompt: There {{blank}} some milk in the fridge.

explanation.zh: milk 不可数，there be 用 is。
explanation.en: Milk is uncountable, so there be takes is.

questions.prompt: I {{blank}} my homework yesterday.

explanation.zh: yesterday 是一般过去时的标志，用 did。
explanation.en: Yesterday marks the simple past, so did is used.

questions.prompt: He is {{blank}} than his brother.

explanation.zh: than 前面用比较级 taller。
explanation.en: Than requires the comparative form taller.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} you like coffee?

explanation.zh: 实义动词 like 的疑问句用 Do 开头。
explanation.en: Questions with the main verb like use Do.

questions.prompt: She has lived here {{blank}} 2019.

explanation.zh: since 接时间点，for 接时间段。
explanation.en: Since takes a point in time; for takes a length of time.

questions.prompt: This is the book {{blank}} I told you about.

explanation.zh: 先行词是物，用 that 或 which；what 不能引导定语从句。
explanation.en: For a thing, use that or which; what cannot introduce a relative clause.

questions.prompt: If it {{blank}} tomorrow, we will stay at home.

explanation.zh: if 条件句用一般现在时表将来。
explanation.en: In a first conditional, the if-clause uses the simple present.

questions.prompt: They {{blank}} TV when I called.

explanation.zh: 过去某一时刻正在做，用过去进行时。
explanation.en: An action in progress at a past moment takes the past continuous.

questions.prompt: In this factory, about two hundred cars {{blank}} every day.

explanation.zh: 主语 cars 是动作的承受者，一般现在时被动语态用 are produced。
explanation.en: The cars receive the action, so the present passive are produced is needed.

questions.prompt: Look at those dark clouds! It {{blank}} rain in a few minutes.

explanation.zh: 有眼前证据的预测用 be going to，主语 it 配 is。
explanation.en: A prediction based on what we can see uses be going to, with is for it.

questions.prompt: Please be quiet. The baby {{blank}} at the moment.

explanation.zh: at the moment 表示此刻正在进行，用现在进行时 is sleeping。
explanation.en: At the moment points to an action happening now, so the present continuous is used.

questions.prompt: My father {{blank}} walks to the office, but today he took the bus.

explanation.zh: 频度副词 usually 放在实义动词前，表示平时如此。
explanation.en: The frequency adverb usually goes before the main verb and marks a habit.

questions.prompt: This film is {{blank}} than the one we saw last week.

explanation.zh: 多音节形容词的比较级用 more + 原级，than 前用 more interesting。
explanation.en: Long adjectives form the comparative with more, and than requires that form.

questions.prompt: The new road is {{blank}} as the old one.

explanation.zh: 肯定句表示「一样……」用 as + 原级 + as。
explanation.en: An affirmative equal comparison uses as + adjective + as.

questions.prompt: What was the weather like on Saturday morning?

explanation.zh: 第一句说 Saturday morning was grey and wet。
explanation.en: The first sentence says the morning was grey and wet.

questions.prompt: Why did Emma stay at home at first?

explanation.zh: 雨一直没停，所以她没有去公园。
explanation.en: The rain did not stop, so she did not go to the park.

questions.prompt: Where did Emma and her dog go?
options: To a cafe near the river

explanation.zh: 他们去了河边的小咖啡馆。
explanation.en: They walked to the small cafe near the river.

questions.prompt: What did Emma have at the cafe?

explanation.zh: 她在咖啡馆吃了热三明治；茶是出门前在家喝的。
explanation.en: She had a warm sandwich there; the tea was at home before she left.

questions.prompt: How many boxes were there in the living room?

explanation.zh: 第一段说客厅里有十二个箱子。
explanation.en: The first paragraph says there were twelve boxes in the living room.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "comfortable" tells us that Mimi was

explanation.zh: 猫睡在旧外套上，comfortable 指它暖和又舒服。
explanation.en: The cat is asleep on an old jacket, so comfortable means warm and relaxed.

questions.prompt: What can we learn about Mimi from the passage?
options: She ate part of the apple cake
She found a quiet place to sleep
She ran away to the garden
She was afraid of the new flat

explanation.zh: 猫躲进空箱子睡着，说明它自己找了个安静角落。
explanation.en: Mimi is asleep in an empty box, so she found a quiet place for herself.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to make an apple cake
A cat that cannot find its food
A family's first day in a new home
A long bus ride across the city

explanation.zh: 全文按时间顺序写搬家第一天的经历与心情。
explanation.en: The text follows one moving day from morning to evening in the new flat.

questions.prompt: Why did Ben take the ticket out of his pocket at the station?
options: To show it to a friend
To put it in his book

explanation.zh: 文中说他拿出车票看座位号，风就在这时把票吹走了。
explanation.en: He took it out to read the number of his seat.

questions.prompt: In the passage, "a big gust" is

explanation.zh: gust 指一阵强风，正是它把票从本手里吹走。
explanation.en: A gust is a sudden strong wind, which pulled the ticket from his hand.

questions.prompt: How did Ben feel after the ticket was gone?

explanation.zh: 他脸红了，又没钱再买票，可见他很着急。
explanation.en: His face went red and he had no money for another ticket, so he was worried.

questions.prompt: What does the story suggest about the woman in the blue coat?
options: She was in a hurry to leave

explanation.zh: 她拾到票主动问本是不是在找，可见她善良又乐于助人。
explanation.en: She picked up the ticket and asked if he was looking for it, so she was kind.

questions.prompt: He {{blank}} his keys, so he could not open the door.

explanation.zh: lost 是「丢了」；丢了钥匙才打不开门。
explanation.en: Lost means he no longer had the keys, so he could not open the door.

questions.prompt: I am very {{blank}} . Can I have a glass of water?

explanation.zh: thirsty 是「渴」，所以想喝水。
explanation.en: Thirsty means needing a drink, which is why water is asked for.

questions.prompt: My sister is a {{blank}} . She works in a hospital.

explanation.zh: nurse 是护士，在医院工作。
explanation.en: A nurse works in a hospital.

questions.prompt: We need to {{blank}} the bus at the next stop because this is our station.

explanation.zh: get off 是「下车」；get on 是「上车」。
explanation.en: Get off means to leave the bus; get on means to board it.

questions.prompt: The film was so {{blank}} that I fell asleep.

explanation.zh: boring 形容事物「令人无聊」；bored 形容人「感到无聊」。
explanation.en: Boring describes the film; bored would describe how a person feels.

questions.prompt: Please {{blank}} the window. It is cold in here.

explanation.zh: 屋里冷，所以要关窗；close 是关上。
explanation.en: It is cold inside, so the window should be closed.

questions.prompt: He is very {{blank}} . He always helps other people.

explanation.zh: kind 是善良、乐于助人。
explanation.en: Kind means caring about other people.

questions.prompt: Can I {{blank}} by card?

explanation.zh: pay by card 是刷卡付款；spend 的主语是人花钱，cost 的主语是物。
explanation.en: Pay by card is the fixed phrase; spend and cost take different subjects.

questions.prompt: The soup is too {{blank}} . Please add some water.

explanation.zh: 太咸才需要加水；salty 是咸的。
explanation.en: Salty soup is the reason to add water.

questions.prompt: Follow the {{blank}} on the box and the cake will be ready in an hour.

explanation.zh: recipe 是食谱，盒子上写着做蛋糕的步骤。
explanation.en: A recipe tells you how to cook something, so it is what you follow on a cake box.

questions.prompt: We had to {{blank}} the picnic because of the heavy rain.

explanation.zh: cancel 是取消，大雨让野餐办不成了。
explanation.en: Cancel means to decide an event will not happen, which is what heavy rain forces.

questions.prompt: The bus was very {{blank}} this morning, so I had to stand all the way.

explanation.zh: crowded 是拥挤的，人多没有座位才要一直站着。
explanation.en: Crowded means full of people, which is why there was no seat.

questions.prompt: Can I {{blank}} your pen for a minute? I forgot mine.

explanation.zh: borrow 是「借入」，我借你的笔；lend 是「借出」。
explanation.en: Borrow means to take something for a short time; lend goes the other way.

questions.prompt: We need to {{blank}}, or we will miss the train.

explanation.zh: hurry 是赶快，不快一点就赶不上火车。
explanation.en: Hurry means to move quickly, which is needed to catch the train.

questions.prompt: My bike is broken. Can you {{blank}} it this afternoon?

explanation.zh: fix 是修理，坏了的东西需要修。
explanation.en: Fix means to repair, which is what a broken bike needs.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film {{blank}} .

explanation.zh: 电影在我们到达之前已经开始，过去的过去用过去完成时。
explanation.en: The film started before we arrived, so the past perfect is used.

questions.prompt: He suggested {{blank}} a taxi.

explanation.zh: suggest 后接动名词：suggest doing。
explanation.en: Suggest is followed by the -ing form.

questions.prompt: I am looking forward to {{blank}} you.

explanation.zh: look forward to 的 to 是介词，后面用动名词。
explanation.en: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows.

questions.prompt: She asked me where I {{blank}} from.

explanation.zh: 主句是过去时 asked，间接引语里动词相应退到过去时 came。
explanation.en: After the past reporting verb asked, the reported verb shifts back to came.

questions.prompt: The letter {{blank}} yesterday.

explanation.zh: 信是被寄出的，且时间是昨天，用一般过去时的被动语态。
explanation.en: The letter receives the action, and the time is past, so use the past passive.

questions.prompt: You {{blank}} smoke here; it is a hospital.

explanation.zh: 医院禁止吸烟，must not 表示「不许」；do not have to 是「不必」。
explanation.en: Smoking is forbidden here: must not. Do not have to means it is not necessary.

questions.prompt: If I {{blank}} more time, I would travel.

explanation.zh: 与现在事实相反的虚拟条件句：if + 过去时，主句 would + 动词原形。
explanation.en: A second conditional uses if + past simple with would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Neither Tom {{blank}} his friends were there.

explanation.zh: neither ... nor ... 是「既不……也不……」的固定搭配。
explanation.en: The fixed pair is neither ... nor ...

questions.prompt: It is the best film I {{blank}} ever seen.

explanation.zh: 最高级后接现在完成时，主语是 I，用 have。
explanation.en: After a superlative, the present perfect follows; the subject I takes have.

questions.prompt: He denied {{blank}} the window.

explanation.zh: deny 后接动名词：deny doing something。
explanation.en: Deny takes the -ing form.

questions.prompt: The more you practise, {{blank}} you become.

explanation.zh: the + 比较级, the + 比较级 表示「越……越……」。
explanation.en: The comparative ... the comparative ... means the more ..., the more ...

questions.prompt: There {{blank}} be a small cinema here, but it closed years ago.

explanation.zh: there used to be 表示「过去曾有」，从句说明现在已不存在。
explanation.en: There used to be describes something that existed in the past but no longer does.

questions.prompt: The last train leaves at eleven, so you had better {{blank}} it.

explanation.zh: had better 后接动词原形，否定式是 had better not do。
explanation.en: Had better takes a bare infinitive, and its negative form is had better not do.

questions.prompt: I would rather you {{blank}} anyone about the plan until Friday.

explanation.zh: would rather 后接从句时，谈现在或将来用过去式表示愿望。
explanation.en: After would rather, a clause about the present or future takes the past form.

questions.prompt: He left the office early {{blank}} catch the last bus home.

explanation.zh: in order to 后接动词原形表示目的；so that 和 in order that 后面要接完整从句。
explanation.en: In order to is followed by a bare infinitive, while so that and in order that need a full clause.

questions.prompt: You {{blank}} me you were coming — I would have cooked something special.

explanation.zh: should have + 过去分词 表示「本该做而没做」；后半句的虚拟语气说明对方并没有提前说。
explanation.en: Should have plus the past participle criticises something that was not done, which the conditional confirms.

questions.prompt: What did Ana bring when she knocked on the writer's door?
options: A map and a list of streets
Two pairs of gloves and an orange bag

explanation.zh: 文中说 Ana 带着两副手套和一个亮橙色袋子来敲门。
explanation.en: The passage says Ana arrived with two pairs of gloves and a bright orange bag.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "dull" is closest in meaning to

explanation.zh: dull 指工作枯燥，与 boring 同义，后文的 but the morning passed quickly 也说明他原本以为会很无聊。
explanation.en: Dull here means boring, as the contrast with the morning passing quickly shows.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about the writer at the end of the passage?
options: The writer was glad to have joined the clean-up
The writer was disappointed by the number of bags
The writer wished the morning had been longer
The writer wanted to be thanked in public

explanation.zh: 结尾看到干净的河水后理解了邻居为什么来敲门，说明他并不后悔参加。
explanation.en: Understanding why Ana knocked shows the writer was pleased to have taken part.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A morning of cleaning that changed how the writer sees the neighbourhood
How to organise a group of thirty people
Why rivers are dirty after the winter
A boy who found a bicycle wheel in the river

explanation.zh: 全文按时间写了一个上午的清理活动，重点落在作者对社区看法的改变。
explanation.en: The text follows one morning of cleaning and ends with the writer's changed view of the neighbourhood.

questions.prompt: What did the writer do two evenings a week for three months?
options: Studied design software at a college
Checked invoices for a furniture company
Taught a class at the local college

explanation.zh: 文中说作者每周两个晚上在当地学院学设计软件，一共三个月。
explanation.en: The writer spent three months learning design software at a local college, two evenings a week.

questions.prompt: In the passage, "relieved" describes a feeling of
options: gladness that a worry has ended

explanation.zh: relieved 指「松了一口气」，作者早就想换工作，所以部门搬走反而让他轻松。
explanation.en: Relieved means glad that something worrying is over, which fits the writer's wish to change.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about learning something new at forty?
options: It is a mistake unless the pay is higher
It is easier than starting at twenty
It is possible if you stop comparing yourself with experienced people
It is possible only if a teacher helps you

explanation.zh: 老师让他不要和已经做了多年的人比较，随后他找到了工作，可见关键在心态。
explanation.en: The teacher's advice about not comparing himself with experienced people leads to his success.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's attitude towards the new job?
options: Glad to have changed, although the job has some disadvantages
Sorry to have left the old company

explanation.zh: 作者承认工资更低、办公室吵闹，但说现在早到是因为自己想去。
explanation.en: The writer admits the lower pay and noisy office but now arrives early because he wants to.

questions.prompt: How often did the bus run?

explanation.zh: 文中说公交一天只有两班，六点以后就不开了。
explanation.en: The passage says the bus came twice a day and stopped running at six.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "peaceful" means

explanation.zh: peaceful 指安静平和，下文说镇上没有电影院、购物中心，几乎没有车。
explanation.en: Peaceful means quiet and calm, which the town without traffic or a cinema confirms.

questions.prompt: Why did Ruth keep looking at her watch?
options: She had arranged to meet a friend
She was waiting for her food to arrive
She was worried about missing the bus
She wanted the fisherman to stop talking

explanation.zh: 钓鱼人讲了半小时，Ruth 不停看表，而作者却不想让他停下，可见她希望谈话结束。
explanation.en: The fisherman talked for half an hour while the writer wanted him to continue, so Ruth was hoping for it to end.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest at the end of the passage?
options: The same weekend can be boring for one person and enjoyable for another
The guidebook was completely wrong about the town
Small towns are better than cities for holidays

explanation.zh: 两人对同一趟旅行的感受完全不同，结尾说 because we were both right 正是这个意思。
explanation.en: The two friends felt differently about the same trip, and the closing line says both were right.

questions.prompt: The company decided to {{blank}} the meeting until next week.

explanation.zh: postpone 是「推迟」，until next week 说明只是改期，不是取消。
explanation.en: Postpone means to move to a later time; until next week shows it is not cancelled.

questions.prompt: He was {{blank}} for the mistake, although it was not his fault.

explanation.zh: although it was not his fault 说明他受到了责怪，blame for 是「因……被责怪」。
explanation.en: The contrast with not his fault shows he was blamed.

questions.prompt: She {{blank}} her teacher's advice and applied for the job, just as he had suggested.

explanation.zh: follow someone's advice 是「听从建议」；她后来申请了工作，说明听了。
explanation.en: Follow advice is the fixed collocation, and applying shows she took it.

questions.prompt: The weather was terrible, but we still {{blank}} the trip: the rain stopped just as we arrived.

explanation.zh: but still 表示转折：天气差，但旅程仍然玩得开心。
explanation.en: But still marks a contrast: bad weather, yet the trip was enjoyed.

questions.prompt: It is {{blank}} to eat so much sugar; doctors advise against it.

explanation.zh: 吃太多糖不健康，unhealthy 是「不健康的」。
explanation.en: Too much sugar is unhealthy.

questions.prompt: He {{blank}} his leg while playing football.

explanation.zh: 讲过去发生的事用一般过去时 broke；break a leg 是「摔断腿」。
explanation.en: A past event takes the simple past broke; break a leg is the collocation.

questions.prompt: The instructions were so {{blank}} that nobody understood them.

explanation.zh: 没人看懂，说明说明书写得令人困惑：confusing 形容事物。
explanation.en: Nobody understood them, so the instructions were confusing.

questions.prompt: We ran out of milk, so I {{blank}} some on my way home.

explanation.zh: pick up 在这里是「顺路买」；take off 是起飞/脱下。
explanation.en: Pick up here means to buy on the way; take off means to remove or depart.

questions.prompt: She is {{blank}} of spiders and runs away whenever she sees one.

explanation.zh: be afraid of 是「害怕」；interested in、aware of、tired of 搭配不同。
explanation.en: Afraid of means frightened by; the other adjectives take different prepositions.

questions.prompt: When the shoes fell apart after a week, the shop agreed to {{blank}} my money in full.

explanation.zh: refund 是商店把钱退还给顾客，in full 说明是全额退款。
explanation.en: To refund is to give money back to a customer, and in full means the whole amount.

questions.prompt: It took us two hours to {{blank}} the top of the hill in the heat.

explanation.zh: reach 是及物动词，后面直接接地点；arrive 要加 at。
explanation.en: Reach takes a place as its object, while arrive would need the preposition at.

questions.prompt: She decided to {{blank}} the job at the bank and sent her CV that afternoon.

explanation.zh: apply for a job 是固定搭配，寄简历说明她是在申请这份工作。
explanation.en: Apply for a job is the fixed phrase, and sending a CV confirms she was applying.

questions.prompt: Mr Lee is {{blank}} the new project, so any questions about it should go to him.

explanation.zh: in charge of 表示「负责」，所以有问题要找他。
explanation.en: In charge of means responsible for, which is why questions go to him.

questions.prompt: I am sorry — I took your coat {{blank}} because the two look exactly the same.

explanation.zh: by mistake 是「不小心拿错」；道歉和两件外套很像都排除了 on purpose。
explanation.en: By mistake means by accident, and the apology rules out on purpose.

questions.prompt: Hardly {{blank}} the room when the phone rang.

explanation.zh: hardly 置句首要部分倒装：had I entered。
explanation.en: A sentence starting with hardly needs inversion: had I entered.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} the bad weather, the match went ahead.

explanation.zh: 空格后是名词短语，用介词 despite；although 后接句子。
explanation.en: A noun phrase follows, so the preposition despite is needed.

questions.prompt: She would rather {{blank}} at home tonight.

explanation.zh: would rather 后接动词原形。
explanation.en: Would rather takes the base verb.

questions.prompt: The report, {{blank}} was published yesterday, caused a stir.

explanation.zh: 非限制性定语从句不能用 that，指物用 which。
explanation.en: A non-defining relative clause cannot use that; which is correct.

questions.prompt: He is said {{blank}} abroad for years.

explanation.zh: 据说他过去多年住在国外，用不定式完成式 to have lived。
explanation.en: The living happened before now, so the perfect infinitive is used.

questions.prompt: Not until midnight {{blank}} the news.

explanation.zh: not until 置句首要部分倒装：did we hear。
explanation.en: A sentence starting with not until needs inversion.

questions.prompt: I wish I {{blank}} more careful yesterday.

explanation.zh: 对过去的遗憾用 wish + 过去完成时。
explanation.en: Regret about the past uses wish + past perfect.

questions.prompt: It is high time we {{blank}} .

explanation.zh: it is high time 后接一般过去时，表示「早该……了」。
explanation.en: It is high time is followed by the past simple.

questions.prompt: The project is expected {{blank}} by June.

explanation.zh: 项目是被完成的，用不定式被动 to be finished。
explanation.en: The project receives the action, so the passive infinitive is used.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} having studied for years, she failed the exam.

explanation.zh: 空格后是动名词短语，用 despite；although 后接完整句子。
explanation.en: An -ing phrase follows, so despite is used.

questions.prompt: Under no circumstances {{blank}} leave the building.

explanation.zh: under no circumstances 置句首要倒装：should you leave。
explanation.en: A negative adverbial at the start requires inversion: should you.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} carefully you plan the trip, the fewer problems you will have.

explanation.zh: the + 比较级, the + 比较级 结构，前半要用 The more carefully。
explanation.en: The comparative pair needs the more carefully ... the fewer ...

questions.prompt: The old bridge {{blank}} twice since the accident, but engineers still check it every month.

explanation.zh: since 要求现在完成时，桥是被修的，所以用被动 has been repaired。
explanation.en: Since requires the present perfect, and the bridge receives the action, so the passive is used.

questions.prompt: It was not until midnight {{blank}} the noise finally stopped.

explanation.zh: 强调句 It was not until ... that ... 必须用 that 连接。
explanation.en: The cleft structure It was not until ... that ... requires that.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} surprised me most was how calm she remained during the interview.

explanation.zh: 主语从句缺主语时用 what 引导，构成 what 伪分裂句。
explanation.en: The subject clause needs what, standing for the thing that surprised me.

questions.prompt: If only I {{blank}} more time to prepare for tomorrow's exam.

explanation.zh: if only 表示对现在或未来的愿望时用一般过去时 had。
explanation.en: If only for a present wish takes the past simple, so had is correct.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about working from home ten years ago?

explanation.zh: 第一句说十年前在家工作 was unusual（不常见）。
explanation.en: The first sentence says it was unusual ten years ago.

questions.prompt: According to the survey, what do people who work alone at home miss?

explanation.zh: 调查说他们想念办公室里非正式的交谈。
explanation.en: The survey says they miss informal conversations from the office.

questions.prompt: Why does the passage say those conversations matter?
options: They produce new ideas and make asking for help easier
They are part of the salary

explanation.zh: 文中说这些交谈常产生新想法，也让人更容易求助。
explanation.en: The passage says they produce ideas and make asking for help easier.

questions.prompt: How have some companies responded to the problem?
options: By asking staff to come in two or three days a week

explanation.zh: 有些公司要求员工每周到办公室两三天。
explanation.en: Some companies ask staff to come in two or three days a week.

questions.prompt: What did the council ask both sides to do last month?

explanation.zh: 第一段说议会要求双方提交书面陈述。
explanation.en: The first paragraph says the council asked both sides to submit written statements.

questions.prompt: In the first paragraph, the responses are described as 'sharper' because they were:

explanation.zh: sharper 在此指语气更尖锐、更有敌意，而不是更短或更准确。
explanation.en: Sharper here means more hostile in tone, not shorter or more accurate.

questions.prompt: What do the bar owners suggest about the people who complain most loudly?
options: They moved into the area after the bars opened
They come from outside the district
They work night shifts in the city

explanation.zh: 酒吧老板指出最响的投诉来自五年前才改成公寓的楼，当时酒吧已经在了。
explanation.en: The owners note the flats were converted only five years ago, after the bars were there.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's attitude in the last paragraph?
options: The bars should close at eleven
The dispute needs measured facts before it can be settled
The council has already chosen the bars' side

explanation.zh: 末段说议会尚未决定、要先测一整季的噪音，可见作者认为需要事实。
explanation.en: The writer stresses the council has not decided and wants measurements first.

questions.prompt: Why did the repair project begin?
options: The library received a grant for repairs
A retired teacher brought in a box of books

explanation.zh: 第二段说项目几乎是因一位退休教师送来一箱书才开始的。
explanation.en: The second paragraph says it began when a retired teacher brought in a box of books.

questions.prompt: In the third paragraph, 'reversible' glue means glue that can be:

explanation.zh: reversible 指修复以后可以撤销，让后来的主人能拆开。
explanation.en: Reversible means the repair can be undone later by another owner.

questions.prompt: Why does the library put a small card inside repaired books?
options: To explain why a copy may look old
To warn readers not to borrow it

explanation.zh: 末段说卡片解释做过什么修复，让读者明白书为何显得更旧。
explanation.en: The card explains what was done, so readers understand why the copy looks older.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of printing in Britain
A volunteer project that keeps old books in use

explanation.zh: 全文讲志愿者修书项目如何让旧书继续被借阅。
explanation.en: The passage is about volunteers repairing books so they stay in use.

questions.prompt: The new policy will {{blank}} all employees.

explanation.zh: affect 是动词「影响」；effect 多作名词「影响、效果」。
explanation.en: Affect is the verb meaning to influence; effect is usually a noun.

questions.prompt: Her explanation was so {{blank}} that everyone was convinced.

explanation.zh: 令人信服的是 explanation，用 -ing 形式的 convincing。
explanation.en: The explanation is the thing that convinces, so convincing is correct.

questions.prompt: The company had to {{blank}} several staff because of the crisis.

explanation.zh: lay off 是裁员；lay out 是布置，lay down 是放下，lay in 是储备。
explanation.en: Lay off means to dismiss staff for economic reasons.

questions.prompt: The evidence is {{blank}} with his story.

explanation.zh: be consistent with 是「与……一致」；persistent 是「坚持的」。
explanation.en: Consistent with means agreeing with; persistent means continuing.

questions.prompt: He has a {{blank}} knowledge of French history.

explanation.zh: thorough 是「透彻的」；through、thought、though 只是拼写相近。
explanation.en: Thorough means complete and detailed; the others are unrelated words.

questions.prompt: The delay was {{blank}} by heavy snow.

explanation.zh: be caused by 是「由……造成」；result 要用 result from，lead 要用 lead to。
explanation.en: Caused by is correct; result takes from and lead takes to.

questions.prompt: She was {{blank}} to admit her mistake, and argued for an hour before she did.

explanation.zh: 承认错误通常不情愿：reluctant to do 是「不愿做」。
explanation.en: Reluctant to admit means unwilling, which fits admitting a mistake.

questions.prompt: The government has promised to {{blank}} the issue.

explanation.zh: address an issue 是「着手处理问题」；adopt 是采纳。
explanation.en: Address an issue means to deal with it.

questions.prompt: The two countries finally reached an {{blank}} after months of talks, and both sides signed it.

explanation.zh: reach an agreement 是「达成协议」的固定搭配。
explanation.en: Reach an agreement is the fixed collocation.

questions.prompt: Because of the storm, the organizers decided to {{blank}} the match until next Saturday.

explanation.zh: postpone 是「推迟」，可与 until next Saturday 连用；cancel 是「取消」，不能再接 until。
explanation.en: Postpone means to move to a later time and works with until; cancel means to call off.

questions.prompt: It took her months to {{blank}} the loss of her job.

explanation.zh: cope with 是「应对、承受」，与 the loss 搭配；look after 是「照顾」。
explanation.en: Cope with means to deal with a difficulty; look after means to take care of.

questions.prompt: Regular exercise is {{blank}} to good health.

explanation.zh: be vital to 表示「对……至关重要」；trivial 是「微不足道的」。
explanation.en: Vital to means essential for; trivial means unimportant.

questions.prompt: The meeting has been {{blank}} until Thursday because the manager is away.

explanation.zh: put off 是「推迟」；put out 是「扑灭」，put away 是「收好」。
explanation.en: Put off means to postpone; put out means to extinguish.

questions.prompt: His health began to {{blank}} after the operation, and he needed daily care.

explanation.zh: deteriorate 是「恶化」，与 health 搭配，后文 daily care 也印证。
explanation.en: Deteriorate means to become worse, which fits health after an operation.

questions.prompt: Were it not for her support last year, we {{blank}} .

explanation.zh: Were it not for 是虚拟条件句的倒装，指过去的事实，主句用 would have done。
explanation.en: Were it not for is an inverted unreal conditional about the past, so would have failed.

questions.prompt: He spoke as though he {{blank}} the whole story.

explanation.zh: as though 后接与过去事实相反的虚拟语气，用过去完成时。
explanation.en: As though takes the past perfect for an unreal past situation.

questions.prompt: No sooner {{blank}} than the lights went out.

explanation.zh: no sooner 置句首用部分倒装，且配过去完成时。
explanation.en: No sooner at the start needs inversion and the past perfect.

questions.prompt: The proposal, {{blank}} merits are obvious, still needs funding.

explanation.zh: 空格后是名词 merits，用关系代词 whose 表示「其优点」。
explanation.en: A noun follows, so the possessive relative pronoun whose is needed.

questions.prompt: Little {{blank}} that he was being watched.

explanation.zh: little 表示否定并置于句首，需要部分倒装。
explanation.en: Negative little at the start triggers inversion.

questions.prompt: If it were not for the volunteers who give up their weekends, the centre {{blank}} to stay open.

explanation.zh: if it were not for 是现在虚拟条件，主句用 would + 动词原形。
explanation.en: If it were not for states a present unreal condition, so the main clause takes would struggle.

questions.prompt: Had it not been for the quick thinking of a passing cyclist, the driver {{blank}} serious injuries.

explanation.zh: Had it not been for 是过去虚拟条件的倒装，主句用 would have done。
explanation.en: Had it not been for is an inverted unreal past condition, so would have suffered follows.

questions.prompt: I wish I {{blank}} so blunt at the meeting; she has barely spoken to me since.

explanation.zh: wish 后接与过去事实相反的愿望，要用过去完成时。
explanation.en: Wish about an unchangeable past event takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: If only we {{blank}} the instructions before assembling the shelves; now we have to take them apart.

explanation.zh: if only 表达对过去事情的懊悔，要用过去完成时。
explanation.en: If only expresses regret about the past and therefore takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: The Danube, {{blank}} flows through four capital cities, is Europe's second-longest river.

explanation.zh: 逗号隔开的非限制性定语从句只能用 which，不能用 that。
explanation.en: A non-restrictive relative clause after a comma can only be introduced by which.

questions.prompt: The scheme, {{blank}} many households depend, was quietly abandoned last month.

explanation.zh: depend 要与介词 on 搭配，介词提到关系代词前时用 on which。
explanation.en: Depend requires the preposition on, which is fronted as on which in the relative clause.

questions.prompt: She is believed {{blank}} the country shortly before the election.

explanation.zh: 不定式动作发生在谓语动词之前，用完成式 to have done。
explanation.en: When the infinitive action happened earlier than the main verb, the perfect infinitive is used.

questions.prompt: The manuscript is thought {{blank}} in the fire of 1666.

explanation.zh: 不定式的完成被动式 to have been done 表示被动的动作先于谓语发生。
explanation.en: The perfect passive infinitive marks a passive event completed before the main verb.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} of the risk, she took out insurance before the trip.

explanation.zh: having been + 过去分词作状语，表示被动的动作先于主句动作发生。
explanation.en: Having been + past participle is a participial clause for a passive event that happened first.

questions.prompt: I object to {{blank}} the room without telling me first.

explanation.zh: 动名词的复合结构要用所有格 his + -ing，不能用主格或不定式。
explanation.en: The gerund takes a possessive determiner (his using), not a subject pronoun or an infinitive.

questions.prompt: What did the study actually report?
options: That all 1,200 pupils should stop using tablets.
That a later bedtime improves vocabulary scores.
That screens permanently damage teenagers' memory.
A weak link between evening screen use and one vocabulary test score.

explanation.zh: 第二段明确说研究只发现晚间屏幕使用与一项词汇测试分数之间的微弱相关。
explanation.en: The second paragraph says the study found only a modest correlation with one vocabulary test.

questions.prompt: In the last paragraph, the word "unglamorous" is closest in meaning to

explanation.zh: unglamorous 在此指答案平淡、不吸引人却实用。
explanation.en: Unglamorous here means plain and unexciting yet sensible.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the newspaper's article?
options: It was corrected before it reached any school.
It quoted the pupils who took part in the research.
It was based on a second, much larger study.
It dropped the authors' warning that the data showed no cause.

explanation.zh: 文中说作者的告诫只出现在论文第四段、报道中完全没有，可推知报道略去了这一限定。
explanation.en: The warning appears in the paper but in none of the coverage, so the article left it out.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best states the writer's main point?
options: Oversimplified research claims spread fast and are hard to undo.
The study was poorly designed and proved nothing.
Parents ought to ban tablets for teenagers.
Journalists should stop reporting on scientific research.

explanation.zh: 全文围绕简化后的结论传播极快、且一旦扩散便难以纠正展开。
explanation.en: The passage is about how quickly a simplified claim travels and how hard it is to correct.

questions.prompt: What does the reviewer say about the exhibition's labels?
options: They explain every object at length.
They were removed after visitors complained.
They were written by the factory inspector.
They give only names and dates.

explanation.zh: 第一段说除了名称和日期之外没有任何墙面说明文字。
explanation.en: The first paragraph states that there are no wall texts beyond names and dates.

questions.prompt: In the third paragraph, "mannerism" is closest in meaning to

explanation.zh: 此处 mannerism 指刻意为之、渐显做作的风格习惯。
explanation.en: Mannerism here means a stylistic habit that begins to look forced.

questions.prompt: What does the reviewer imply about the final room?
options: Its short timeline concedes that context was needed.
It was added at the last minute without the curator.
It holds the most valuable objects in the show.
It is the only room visitors tend to skip.

explanation.zh: 作者说最后一间展室提供简短时间内线却最有趣，其简短更像一种「承认」。
explanation.en: The reviewer calls the final room's brevity an admission rather than a stylistic choice.

questions.prompt: The reviewer's overall attitude to the exhibition is best described as
options: admiring, though doubtful about its refusal to explain.
enthusiastic with no reservations at all.
dismissive and impatient with the whole show.
unsure whether the objects are genuine.

explanation.zh: 作者称展览「用心、值得」，同时批评其拒绝提供背景，态度是欣赏中带保留。
explanation.en: The reviewer praises the show as thoughtful while criticising its lack of context.

questions.prompt: Why may clinics now favour video appointments?
options: They require no trained staff at all.
They are paid at the same rate as in-person visits but cost less to provide.
Patients refuse to travel to clinics for any appointment.
Video calls allow doctors to examine patients more thoroughly.

explanation.zh: 第二段指出视频问诊与人面对面问诊报销比例相同，成本却更低，因而更有利可图。
explanation.en: Video visits are reimbursed at the same rate as in-person ones yet are cheaper to deliver.

questions.prompt: In the final paragraph, "nostalgia" is closest in meaning to
options: a sentimental longing for the way things were.
a fear of using new technology.
relief that the emergency is over.

explanation.zh: nostalgia 指对过去诊疗方式的怀旧式眷恋，与「一味热情」相对。
explanation.en: Nostalgia means a sentimental attachment to the old way of doing things.

questions.prompt: The rule brought in by two health boards suggests that
options: remote appointments are always the cheapest option.
doctors are reluctant to learn new technology.
some conditions cannot be assessed reliably at a distance.
patients dislike speaking to doctors on screen.

explanation.zh: 要求连续三次远程问诊后必须面诊，说明某些诊断需要当面检查，可推知远程评估有局限。
explanation.en: Requiring an in-person review after three remote visits implies distance has limits for some diagnoses.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarises the writer's argument?
options: Telemedicine is too costly to be worth continuing.
Telemedicine should be used selectively and paid for according to need, not convenience.
Telemedicine was a temporary wartime measure and should now end.
Telemedicine should replace nearly all face-to-face care.

explanation.zh: 结尾主张把远程医疗当作多种工具之一，按病人需要选用，并避免按便利程度付费。
explanation.en: The writer wants telemedicine treated as one tool among several, chosen by need rather than convenience.

questions.prompt: The report was {{blank}} with inconsistencies.

explanation.zh: be riddled with 是「满是（问题）」的固定搭配。
explanation.en: Riddled with means full of something bad, a fixed collocation.

questions.prompt: His argument was {{blank}} , relying on assumptions rather than evidence.

explanation.zh: tenuous 是「薄弱的」；tenacious 是「顽强的」，tedious 是「冗长的」。
explanation.en: Tenuous means weak or thin, which matches an argument built on assumptions.

questions.prompt: The committee's decision was met with {{blank}} criticism.

explanation.zh: scathing criticism 是「严厉的批评」。
explanation.en: Scathing criticism is severe and harsh.

questions.prompt: She has an {{blank}} ability to remember names.

explanation.zh: uncanny 是「不可思议的」，常形容能力出奇。
explanation.en: Uncanny means strange and remarkable, often of an ability.

questions.prompt: The reforms were introduced {{blank}} , without consulting teachers and with no clear plan.

explanation.zh: haphazardly 是「随意地、杂乱地」，与没有征询意见相呼应。
explanation.en: Haphazardly means without plan or order, matching the lack of consultation.

questions.prompt: Coastal towns bore the {{blank}} of the storm, while inland villages escaped the worst of it.

explanation.zh: bear the brunt of 意为「承受……的主要冲击」，是固定搭配。
explanation.en: Bear the brunt of means to suffer the main force of something.

questions.prompt: Years of night shifts had taken a heavy {{blank}} on her health.

explanation.zh: take a toll on 意为「对……造成损害」，是固定搭配。
explanation.en: Take a toll on means to cause damage or harm over time.

questions.prompt: In the {{blank}} of the scandal, three ministers resigned within a week.

explanation.zh: in the wake of 意为「在……之后、随之而来」。
explanation.en: In the wake of means following or as a result of an event.

questions.prompt: Cut off by the floods, the village was left at the {{blank}} of the river.

explanation.zh: at the mercy of 意为「任……摆布、受……支配」。
explanation.en: At the mercy of means completely in the power of something else.

questions.prompt: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in {{blank}}.

explanation.zh: a blessing in disguise 指「因祸得福」。
explanation.en: A blessing in disguise is something bad that turns out to be good.

questions.prompt: He sent a long letter to make {{blank}} for his rudeness at dinner.

explanation.zh: make amends for 意为「为……赔罪、弥补」。
explanation.en: Make amends for means to apologise and compensate for a wrong.

questions.prompt: On match days parking near the stadium is at a {{blank}}, and drivers willingly pay three times the usual rate.

explanation.zh: at a premium 意为「稀缺而昂贵」，与后文付三倍价钱呼应。
explanation.en: At a premium means scarce and therefore expensive.

questions.prompt: The new evidence bears {{blank}} her original claim that the drug was safe.

explanation.zh: bear out 是「证实、支持（某种说法）」的固定搭配。
explanation.en: Bear out means to confirm or support a claim.

questions.prompt: A knee injury in training put {{blank}} to his chances of playing in the final.

explanation.zh: put paid to 是英式固定说法，意为「使……彻底落空」。
explanation.en: Put paid to means to put a definite end to something.

questions.prompt: The inspectors broke the rules with {{blank}}, confident that no one would ever report them.

explanation.zh: with impunity 意为「不受惩罚地」，与后文「确信无人举报」呼应。
explanation.en: With impunity means without any fear of punishment.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} he apologized, she refused to speak to him.

explanation.zh: much as 引导让步，意思是「尽管……」。
explanation.en: Much as introduces a concession meaning although.

questions.prompt: The manuscript, {{blank}} long been thought lost, reappeared in 1998.

explanation.zh: having long been thought lost 是完成分词短语，作后置修饰。
explanation.en: Having long been thought lost is a perfect participial phrase modifying the manuscript.

questions.prompt: Had it not been for his intervention, the deal {{blank}} .

explanation.zh: Had it not been for 是与过去事实相反的倒装虚拟，主句用 would have done。
explanation.en: Had it not been for is an inverted past unreal conditional, so would have collapsed.

questions.prompt: Such {{blank}} the force of the storm that windows shattered.

explanation.zh: such 置句首构成倒装，主语是 the force，谓语用 was。
explanation.en: Such at the start inverts the clause; the subject force takes was.

questions.prompt: He resented {{blank}} to justify every decision.

explanation.zh: resent 后接动名词；此处指过去的事，用 having to。
explanation.en: Resent takes the -ing form; having to refers to the past obligation.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} the scholarship, she would be working in a shop now.

explanation.zh: if it were not for 是虚拟条件固定式，表示「若不是」；单独 were it not 缺 for。
explanation.en: If it were not for is the fixed unreal conditional; were it not needs for to be complete.

questions.prompt: He spoke of the city {{blank}} there for years, though he had never left the province.

explanation.zh: as though 后接与过去事实相反的虚拟，用过去完成 had lived。
explanation.en: As though takes the past perfect for a past counterfactual, hence had lived.

questions.prompt: He resented {{blank}} consulted before the decision was announced.

explanation.zh: resent 接动名词，否定词 not 置于 -ing 之前，构成 not being consulted。
explanation.en: Resent takes an -ing form, and not precedes it to give not being consulted.

questions.prompt: The minister's {{blank}} the report before publication was widely criticised.

explanation.zh: 所有格 the minister's 之后必须用动名词 suppressing 作主语中心词。
explanation.en: A possessive such as the minister's requires the gerund suppressing as its head.

questions.prompt: The report examines the extent {{blank}} local councils were consulted before the decision.

explanation.zh: the extent 后固定接 to which，介词由先行词与从句的搭配决定。
explanation.en: Extent selects the preposition to, giving the fixed frame the extent to which.

questions.prompt: There is no such thing {{blank}} a neutral algorithm.

explanation.zh: such ... as 结构里 as 充当关系代词，引出同位成分。
explanation.en: In the such ... as frame, as acts as a relative pronoun introducing the example.

questions.prompt: It was the treasurer {{blank}} signed the cheque, not the chairman.

explanation.zh: 强调句 it was ... who 突出主语 the treasurer，指人用 who 并在从句中作主语。
explanation.en: This is an it-cleft on a person; who is the subject of the relative clause.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} surprised everyone was not the verdict but the speed with which it came.

explanation.zh: what 引导伪分裂句主语从句，等于 the thing that surprised everyone。
explanation.en: What heads a pseudo-cleft subject clause meaning the thing that surprised everyone.

questions.prompt: {{blank}} had the words left her mouth than she regretted them.

explanation.zh: no sooner ... than 是否定词前置倒装，hardly 需搭配 when。
explanation.en: No sooner pairs with than in negative inversion; hardly would require when.

questions.prompt: The abbey is believed {{blank}} in the ninth century and rebuilt on the same site.

explanation.zh: 修道院是被建造的且早于现在，需用完成被动不定式 to have been founded。
explanation.en: The abbey was founded earlier and passively, so the perfect passive infinitive is required.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to a memory once it has been told?
options: It is gradually replaced by pure invention.
It takes on a structure it did not have before.
It becomes more vivid at the edges.

explanation.zh: 第一段说讲过一次后记忆就获得形状（开头、中段、结尾）。
explanation.en: Paragraph one says a told memory acquires a shape of beginning, middle and end.

questions.prompt: In the second paragraph, the word "hardens" most nearly means that the shape of the story
options: becomes fixed and hard to revise.

explanation.zh: hardens 指叙述定形后难以改动，故作者分不清记忆与讲述。
explanation.en: Hardens means the narrative settles and resists revision, blurring memory and telling.

questions.prompt: The author implies that a memoirist who is certain of every detail is
options: unusual, since most writers doubt themselves.
more trustworthy, because the memory has been tested.
less trustworthy, because the certainty has gone unexamined.

explanation.zh: 末段说承认门可能是蓝色的作者更可信，因为前者察觉了叙述机制。
explanation.en: The last paragraph trusts the writer who admits uncertainty, having noticed the machinery.

questions.prompt: Which best captures the author's attitude towards memoir?
options: It matters less than the documents it draws on.
It has been damaged by writers who invent convenient details.
Its value lies in reckoning with a life rather than recording it.
It should be read as fiction, since memory cannot be trusted.

explanation.zh: 作者说读回忆录不是为了记录而是为了清算与反思。
explanation.en: The author reads memoirs for the reckoning, not for the record.

questions.prompt: What does the author say the recommender actually learns?
options: The titles we abandon most quickly.
Our taste as it was before we used the service.
The preferences we state in surveys.
A record of choices we have made, including accidental ones.

explanation.zh: 首段说系统学到的不是品味而是妥协史，连偶然点开的那部片也算在内。
explanation.en: Paragraph one says it learns a history of compromises, accidental choices included.

questions.prompt: The phrase "a history of compromises" suggests that our viewing record
options: reflects incidental choices as much as deliberate ones.
proves that we settle for second best.
is shorter than we tend to imagine.
reveals a hidden appetite for conflict.

explanation.zh: 所谓妥协指在航班上随手看完、十一分钟就关掉这类非刻意选择。
explanation.en: The compromises are the film finished on a flight and the one abandoned after minutes.

questions.prompt: The remark that a recommendation engine is "a mirror that flatters by agreeing" implies that it
options: confirms our existing habits while seeming to broaden our choices.
treats agreement as the surest sign of good taste.
praises users in order to keep them subscribed.
is deliberately built to deceive its users.

explanation.zh: 镜子只反映既有偏好，并把这种收窄说成发现。
explanation.en: The mirror only reflects existing preferences and reports the narrowing as discovery.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the author's position?
options: Users should be shown the weights behind every recommendation.
Recommendation engines ought to be abolished outright.
Machine learning is incapable of modelling anyone's taste.
Transparency alone cannot fix a system that narrows the culture it feeds.

explanation.zh: 作者承认公开模型有用但 insufficient，主张系统应提供未被要求的东西。
explanation.en: The author calls transparency useful but insufficient, preferring systems that surprise us.

questions.prompt: According to the author, what usually happens to existing residents after a district is "saved"?
options: They are invited to help plan the restoration.
They leave once rents rise, having never been consulted.
They are hired by the businesses that move in.
They return once the repairs are complete.

explanation.zh: 首段说居民未被咨询，租金翻倍后他们已不在那里可被咨询。
explanation.en: Paragraph one notes they are not consulted, and after rents double they are no longer there.

questions.prompt: In the second paragraph, "unglamorous" is used to describe
options: rules that are easy for owners to evade.
residents who refuse to cooperate with planners.
practical measures that attract little public attention.

explanation.zh: unglamorous 修饰租金管制、租约、长椅这类不体面却实用的措施。
explanation.en: It modifies rent controls, a lease and a bench: useful measures with no photogenic appeal.

questions.prompt: By asking what the district is like on "a wet Tuesday in February", the author is testing whether
options: the repairs have protected the buildings from bad weather.
the council has provided adequate drainage.
the shops stay open at unseasonable hours.
ordinary daily life continues there, not only the visitor's experience.

explanation.zh: 作者以淡季雨天的日常检验街区是否还有生活，而非只有游客视角。
explanation.en: A wet off-season Tuesday tests ordinary life rather than the visitor's impression.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarises the column's argument?
options: Historic districts should be left entirely unregulated.
Heritage tourism is the most reliable way to fund repairs.
Chains should be banned from restored neighbourhoods.
Preservation should protect the routines of a place, not only its buildings.

explanation.zh: 末段点题：遗产不是建筑，而是使用它的习惯。
explanation.en: The closing line states that heritage is not the building but the habit of using it.

questions.prompt: The article's tone was {{blank}} , mocking the author without naming him.

explanation.zh: sardonic 是「冷嘲的」，与 mocking 同义；sanguine 是乐观的。
explanation.en: Sardonic means mocking in a dry way; sanguine means optimistic.

questions.prompt: Her apology seemed {{blank}} , more a formality than a regret.

explanation.zh: perfunctory 是「例行公事般的」，与 more a formality 一致。
explanation.en: Perfunctory means done as a routine duty, matching a mere formality.

questions.prompt: The two accounts are {{blank}} , each contradicting the other.

explanation.zh: irreconcilable 是「无法调和的」，所以互相矛盾。
explanation.en: Irreconcilable means impossible to make consistent, hence contradictory.

questions.prompt: He is known for his {{blank}} remarks, often offending without intent.

explanation.zh: caustic 是「尖刻的」，与伤人相呼应；cryptic 是隐晦的。
explanation.en: Caustic means bitterly sharp; cryptic means mysterious.

questions.prompt: The government's response was widely seen as {{blank}} , avoiding any firm commitment.

explanation.zh: equivocal 是「含糊其辞的」；unequivocal 才是明确，正好相反。
explanation.en: Equivocal means ambiguous; unequivocal is its opposite.

questions.prompt: The committee's report was {{blank}}: it offered no recommendation and left every question open.

explanation.zh: inconclusive 是「无定论的」，与「未给出建议、把所有问题都留着」一致。
explanation.en: Inconclusive means reaching no conclusion, matching a report that recommends nothing.

questions.prompt: The court found the penalty {{blank}}: it was far harsher than the offence warranted.

explanation.zh: disproportionate 是「不成比例的」，正是「比罪行应有的严厉得多」。
explanation.en: Disproportionate means out of proportion, exactly the mismatch between penalty and offence.

questions.prompt: Nothing had been written down, yet a {{blank}} agreement existed that the subject would never be raised.

explanation.zh: tacit 指「默契的、未言明的」，与 nothing had been written down 呼应；taciturn 只形容人沉默。
explanation.en: Tacit describes an unspoken understanding; taciturn merely describes a silent person.

questions.prompt: The board {{blank}} to the chairman's proposal without a single objection.

explanation.zh: accede to 是固定搭配，意为「同意、接受」，且只有它能接 to。
explanation.en: Accede to is the fixed collocation meaning to agree; the other verbs do not take to here.

questions.prompt: Even a {{blank}} reading of the contract would have revealed the clause.

explanation.zh: cursory 是「草率的、粗略的」，与 even 引出的最低要求相合。
explanation.en: Cursory means hurried and superficial, the minimum effort that would still have sufficed.

questions.prompt: The book is less a record of events than a {{blank}} on the nature of memory.

explanation.zh: meditation on 意为「对……的沉思随笔」，正合「不是记事而是论记忆」。
explanation.en: A meditation on something is a reflective piece of writing, not a record of events.

questions.prompt: She felt {{blank}} about the offer, drawn by the salary yet unwilling to relocate.

explanation.zh: ambivalent 指「（对某事的）矛盾心情」，与既心动又抗拒的两面并列呼应。
explanation.en: Ambivalent means holding conflicting feelings; ambiguous describes wording, not a person's mind.

questions.prompt: A small bonus was offered to {{blank}} the staff, though the grievance itself was never addressed.

explanation.zh: placate 是「安抚、平息」，与给奖金却未解决问题的手段相合。
explanation.en: Placate means to calm someone down, which a token bonus is meant to do.

questions.prompt: His support for the scheme was {{blank}}: he voted for it but did nothing to defend it.

explanation.zh: lukewarm 引申为「不冷不热的、勉强的」，与投票却不辩护的行为一致。
explanation.en: Lukewarm support is unenthusiastic, matching a vote cast but never defended.

questions.prompt: The new evidence {{blank}} the researcher, whose findings had been dismissed for a decade.

explanation.zh: vindicate 是「证明……清白/正确」，与十年来成果被否定形成反转。
explanation.en: Vindicate means to clear someone of doubt or blame, reversing years of dismissal.
